entry.title: Taking care of something growing
entry.summary: Davies includes watering, leaf care, and arranging flowers as ways toddlers can join the care of a home. Interest, manageable tools, and adult help shape the part they take.
entry.cue: Notice an interest in leaves, flowers, carrying a little water, or the work you do for a plant.
detail: Her watering row specifically includes steady walking. Leaf care is another possibility: she describes a small sponge or plant duster. She also includes growing vegetables in pots for homes without a garden.

For flowers, the book uses stems already cut to length, small vases, a little jug and funnel, and a sponge for spills. Your child may be interested only in pouring or wiping at first; the complete arrangement can wait.
Her gardening examples include planting and ongoing care. They are examples of shared work, with supervision for small parts and sharp tools, rather than a requirement to maintain a garden.
